A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PID-based Spuriousness Disentangler research, retaining identifiable theory and Waterbird/Dominoes experiments despite substantial revision. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original PID estimates, classification accuracies and Grad-CAM results for Waterbird and two Dominoes variants in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations across six datasets, including new tabular and multiclass experiments, quantitative localization results and sensitivity analyses in Section 5 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: v2 replaces unique spurious-feature information alone with Msp = Uni(Y:B|F) - Uni(Y:F|B) - Syn(Y:F,B). It adds automatic CLIPSeg/FPN segmentation and alternative estimation routes, including multiclass PID estimation. The autoencoder reconstruction/clustering objective and Waterbird bottleneck already existed in v1 and are not new components.

E1.justification: Waterbird and both Dominoes variants are retained. v2 adds Adult income prediction, CelebAMask-HQ hair-color classification, Spawrious dog-breed classification, and binary/ten-class Colored MNIST. Coverage also expands to unavailable segmentation masks and non-spatial color biases, substantially broadening domains and input conditions.

E2.justification: v2 adds focused numerical comparisons against I(Y;B) and I(Y;B)-I(Y;F) in Table 2, plus DIT versus Liang et al. PID estimators on binary CMNIST in Figure 24. v1 does not report corresponding comparisons; its stated PCA comparison is not accompanied by identifiable comparative results.

E3.justification: v2 adds class-balanced and additional random-split Waterbird evaluations, IoU measurement, cluster-count sweeps and CMNIST flip-rate protocols. Waterbird autoencoder training changes from 150 pretraining plus 50 training epochs to 50 plus 100. The reported Dominoes 2.0 Group 11 training count changes from 3,000 to 300. v2 also describes worst-group evaluation across groups, replacing v1's explicit fixed-minority/averaging description. These are reported revisions, not proof that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond retained balancing, background-mixing and Grad-CAM analyses, v2 adds quantitative mask alignment using IoU, cluster-count sensitivity and runtime/convergence analysis, and sensitivity to PID-estimator choice (Tables 1, 3–4; Figures 16 and 24). These directly examine localization validity, representation stability and computational limitations absent from v1.

E5.justification: v2 introduces +/- reporting for worst-group accuracies in Tables 7–8 and Pearson correlations with p-values in Figures 7 and 14; v1 reports point estimates and descriptive trends. This statistical reporting remains limited: v2 does not identify what +/- represents or specify repetition counts or seeds, so additional runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: v2 adds Msp values, results for four additional datasets and new diagnostic analyses. Earlier accuracy summaries also change: unbalanced Waterbird is 29.75% in v1 Table 1 and 45.92 +/- 1.43% in v2 Table 7. Most earlier PID components recur with rounding in v2 Table 6, while v1's mean-accuracy panel is removed. Revised settings and reporting prevent treating changed accuracies as controlled performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix C add the Msp definition, candidate measures and counterexamples, Gaussian redundancy/synergy lemmas, a noisy-feature information bound and Bayes-classifier derivations. v2 also proves feature-transfer monotonicity. The earlier Blackwell-equivalence argument is retained, including its stochastic-matrix proof as Lemma 7, rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: The central claim changes from unique spurious-feature information being the spuriousness measure to a broader explanation of four dependency types and a signed measure incorporating core information and synergy. v2 emphasizes anticipating optimal-classifier feature preferences and removes v1's asserted superiority of its autoencoder estimator over classical estimators.

C2.justification: v2 develops substantive interpretations of redundancy as allowing either feature and synergy as enabling spurious features to denoise core features. It explicitly distinguishes Bayes-optimal predictions from actual trained-model accuracy. Appendix A expands limitations to subjective feature categorization, sample-complexity and optimization difficulties, unresolved estimation error and interactions among multiple spurious-feature groups.

D1.justification: v2 adds algorithm pseudocode, segmentation prompts and pretrained-model details, estimator choices, runtime measurements, cluster-selection guidance and a code-access link. Conversely, v1's layer-by-layer architecture table and detailed Waterbird architecture diagram disappear, along with explicit 70/30 splitting, weighted-sampling and numerical stopping-threshold disclosures. These are substantial changes in reproducibility information, not necessarily changes to every underlying procedure.

R1.justification: The central positioning of applying PID to dataset spuriousness remains. v2 adds focused connections to feature-separation and Gaussian-separability research, dataset documentation, and PID-estimation limitations and alternatives. It also explicitly attributes the retained stochastic-matrix lemma to Bertschinger et al. (2014), refining attribution and positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten around dataset explainability and the revised measure. v1's combined main-results section becomes separate theory and methodology sections; experiments are reorganized around feature-availability scenarios, and limitations and broader impacts receive dedicated appendices. This substantially changes the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 switches the main text from two columns to one, redraws and separates the framework diagrams, and adds an algorithm box and canonical-dependency illustration. Experimental displays are reorganized with Msp axes, logarithmic PID scales and expanded tables; new diagnostic plots appear. Earlier detailed architecture displays are removed, not merely relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens conceptual justification through explicit counterexamples and treatment of core information, redundancy and synergy. Evaluations beyond v1's two image datasets, quantitative localization checks and estimator/cluster sensitivity analyses address important validation gaps. Clearer applicability limits also improve interpretation. Lost architecture detail and undefined uncertainty notation weaken reproducibility, but the gains in justification and empirical scrutiny outweigh those losses.
